Port S3: easier setups to tap, and the partial cost

The answer first: I recommend giving each machining setup its own card with a header band that says "Show on model ›" and turns blue with "Shown on model" when it is picked (option A). Please reply in chat with four answers: Q1 to Q4 below. Everything else on this page is shown so you can see it; say if anything should change.

The screenshots are the real app on real test parts with the new styles applied to the page; the pocket line, the not-checked line on Cost and the “(partial)” words are added by hand to show the browser copy, because S3 is not built yet.

Setups: today and two options

Q1. Which setup look? A (recommended: the band makes each setup read as one thing to tap, and the picked one is plain to see) · B · keep today's.
Q2. Should the new setup look also go into the Python app on your PC? Yes (recommended: one look for both, and the browser copy replaces it at S8) · Only the browser copy (both copies share one style sheet, so this needs a build switch).

Machining in the browser copy: pockets are not in its plan yet

Until S4 the browser copy does not find pockets, so its plan holds only the holes. On a part with pockets it would show too few setups and tools, with nothing saying so. The engine can't tell which parts have pockets yet, so the line shows on every milled part until S4.

Q3. Show this line on Machining until pockets are ported (S4)? Yes, as worded: “Pockets are not in this plan yet in this copy, so it may need more setups and tools.” (recommended) · Yes, with your words · No line.

Cost: the total reads “(partial)”

While a check that feeds a cost driver (corner radius, pocket depth, undercut, thin wall) has not run, the total reads “(partial)”, and the not-checked line used on Features and Report is added to the Cost step, above the drivers (a new place for it). On a milled part that is every part until S5.

Q4. Add the “Total score” line to the PDF? The PDF has no total today; the spec asks for the total to read “(partial)” in the PDF, so it needs one. Yes, in both copies, without “(partial)” in the Python app (recommended: one PDF layout) · Only the browser copy · No total line in the PDF.

  • A part with no cost drivers shows today's “None: one setup and no tools to load.” plus the not-checked line; no total, so no “(partial)”.
  • The setup chips over the model stay as they are; only the side list changes.
